speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance and distribution of the itchy rash, and confirm if it started shortly after you began taking the antibiotics? Also, how high has the fever gotten, and which joints are most painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any swelling or hives (angioedema), particularly around your lips or eyes, when the rash first appeared? Also, have you had any difficulty breathing or any pain in your abdomen or blood in your urine?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance Normal, WBC Within normal limits, RBC Within normal limits, Protein Negative, Glucose Negative. Complete_Blood_Count: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal urinalysis and blood count help rule out serious complications like Henoch-Schönlein purpura or sepsis. Given the timing after amoxicillin and the joint pain, this looks like a serum sickness-like reaction; do you have any swollen lymph nodes or red eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diagnosed with acute sinusitis one week ago, no known history of adverse drug reactions, immunizations up to date. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming those details. Based on the timing after amoxicillin, the rash distribution, joint pain, and normal lab results, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Serum sickness-like reaction
